title: Blender MCP can oneshot animations... with a twist
author: dx0ne
selftext:
Wait for it....

I wanted to test the Belnder MCP for Claude(Opus) - pointed it to model generated via Meshy. It opened Blender, imported mesh, rigged, animated and rendered video preview. Was ok as a tempshit anim without and hand work. Then I looked into the scene...

I find it hilarious - it invented kind of"ballerina" illussion. Again - as a filler for game prototype that will probably end up in the bin? Perfect.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body:
well. it set the groundwork and you would only have to tweak a bit without having to mess with bones, uv maps , etc. 

i call this a plus but will still wait another yewar till i touch 3d with AI

replies.author: dx0ne
replies.body: In general I agree - as in "it's not production ready" - but lot of time(=money) is wasted during early phases to create assets or waiting for temp assets. This opens way to faster iteration and to the holy grail of production of iterative work - ability to fail faster. This comes from someone who spent years being art producer in aaa projects. Ofc adoption of such pipelines is almost non existent.

replies.author: Belmeez
replies.body:
I’m actually curious why we think this is unusable? Kind you just tweak it a bit and then import it into your game and it’s good to go?

Sorry I am a noob

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body:
ofc u can do that. 

do that for all 300 animations in your game. 

i personally pass and will wait for more polished AI animations.

replies.author: Belmeez
replies.body: Oh I see you just want to touch anything? Just straight one shotting ai games?

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body:
oh i see you never had a game witrh enough scope that working on animations becomes tedious. ai messes up blending, positioning, coherent look, then with enough scope it no longer understands the whole code it works with but only small bits so errors it secretly made on the way can no longer be repaired with simply copy pasting the error log etc.

and the worst offender is animations. because you intuitively see every flaw as a human. 

no thanks. noone is stopping you, but i aint touching that until its refined.

replies.author: Belmeez
replies.body: Ok I sense that you’re pretty snippy lol I was t challenging you just trying to understand the hidden pitt falls. I did say I was a noob

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body:
ok from my experience:

it looks easy, and it is for one or two animations. but when the scope gets large and you notice that you need useful standards for everything and every animation, it can quickly become a nightmare of "80% of the time you try to fix things ai messed up or doesnt get right".

and when you are doing 3d with animations like op+, then probably the scope is large enough that AI WILL start to mess itself up and you become more of a therapeut and doctor for the ai to fix its own mistakes than an actual game dev.

so to not make that happen i can advice not using ai animations for the time being. and generally plan agames with a scope that can live with "simple" grafics. simply because we are not there yet that is becomes more helpfull than harmfull/workload afterwards-intensive in the visual department.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: Even if it was walking in the correct direction the animation looks like crap. Someone that knows what they are doing could make this in minutes. Would you pay for a game where someone had spent minutes making the most low effort animations possible. It's fine for a prototype but it's not good.

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: What I have found is that one shot is no good, so include a review and second pass. I did this with mesh generation as well but it's almost always better after a review with adjustments, but it can even do some of that itself.

replies.author: dx0ne
replies.body: True that but... so it is with humans :)

comments.author: CubeUnleashed
comments.body: well... they tried. \*watches zombie slowly moonwalking away into the dark night\*

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: have claude take pictures of key frames and insert arrows for forward directio and have it review the them, having claude do checks like this catches this stuff.

replies.author: dx0ne
replies.body: Yes - basically second prompt fixed it. As a throwaway? - good enough.

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: It really can't. You chose like the easiest animation. I tried a more complex one yesterday and it couldn't do it at *all.*

replies.author: dx0ne
replies.body: Maybe. Didnt test it trougly but i ned it only for simple temp anims. The more complicated ones its better to get from video at like move.ai

comments.author: Grandrcp
comments.body: How did you use Claude with Blender?

replies.author: dx0ne
replies.body: There's official mcp server. /mcp in cc or Connectors-Extensions in desktop

replies.author: tuptain
replies.body: My Claude runs my local Blender via command line headless.

replies.author: Grandrcp
replies.body: but is the result good? Because I get terrible results

replies.author: tuptain
replies.body: You have to do multiple passes and tell it what it did wrong. It can't do it by itself yet.
